title: Senior asks: checkAction() uses isset() on ACTION_METHODS. What does this print if one value is null?
explain: isset() is false when the value is null, even if the key exists. array_key_exists() only checks the key. Today all values are strings, so isset() works. If someone adds a null value later, that action would look unknown. Use array_key_exists() when null is a possible value.

title: Senior asks: getFileName() uses basename(). What does this print?
explain: basename() only removes the folder part. A trailing slash is ignored, "/" gives an empty string, and ".." stays "..". So basename is not a full check. Your other checks (extension, is_file) must still reject empty and odd names.

title: Senior asks: storage/ has fruits.csv. On Linux someone calls ?action=read&file=FRUITS.CSV. What happens?
explain: FileService uses strtolower() on the extension, so CSV passes as a known format. But Linux file names are case-sensitive: FRUITS.CSV does not exist, so you get FileNotFoundException and 404. On a default Mac it would work. That is a classic "works on my machine" bug.

pr.title: Use file_exists in checkFileExists
pr.author: olha
pr.body: The name file_exists is clearer than is_file, and it is the same check.

explain: It is not the same check. file_exists() is also true for folders. A folder named old.csv in storage would pass, and the next step fails with a confusing error (usually 500) instead of a clear 404. is_file() is true only for regular files. Keep it.

title: PHP 8. A function returns null by mistake. What does this print?
code:
<?php
function rows(): ?array { return null; }
try {
    echo count(rows());
} catch (TypeError $e) {
    echo 'TypeError';
}
explain: In PHP 7, count(null) gave a warning and 1 or 0. Since PHP 8, count() accepts only arrays and Countable objects, so null throws a TypeError. This is good: the bug shows up at once. Check for null first, or make the function return an empty array.

title: What does Node print?
explain: The spread { ...a } is a shallow copy. Simple values like name are copied. The nested object opts is shared, so b.opts.v = 2 also changes a. Use structuredClone(a) for a deep copy.

title: Link previews and search bots delete posts. Tap the bug.
explain: The route has no methods, so a simple GET link deletes the post. Bots, prefetch and link previews follow GET links. Another site can also trigger it (CSRF). Allow only POST and check a CSRF token before you remove anything.

title: A bad commit is on shared main and colleagues already pulled it. How do you undo it safely?
options: git reset --hard HEAD~1, then git push --force
git revert <commit>, then a normal git push
explain: git revert adds a new commit that undoes the bad one. History stays the same, so colleagues can just pull. reset or amend plus force-push rewrites shared history and breaks other people's branches. Rewrite history only on your own unpushed work.
